title: Terraform + EKS
tagline: Provision TiDB Cloud, AWS EKS, and an app in one terraform apply
pattern: Platform teams that provision everything with Terraform on AWS and EKS, and want to see a database fit their IaC workflow, including how dedicated or bring-your-own-cloud style deployments are scripted.

metrics.label: Resources planned
metrics.howMeasured: Count of planned_change messages from terraform plan -json

metrics.label: Resources created
metrics.howMeasured: Count of distinct apply_complete hook.resource.addr values from terraform apply -json

metrics.label: Per-resource apply time
metrics.howMeasured: hook.elapsed_seconds from each resource's apply_complete message

metrics.label: Total apply time
metrics.howMeasured: Wall-clock time from spawning terraform apply to process exit 0, via runner-kit timed()

metrics.label: App query rate
metrics.howMeasured: Load generator's completed-request count per 1000ms tick against the app /work endpoint

metrics.label: App p99 latency
metrics.howMeasured: Load generator's per-request latency sample window, summarize() p99 each tick

metrics.label: Errors during scale change
metrics.howMeasured: Load generator's failed-request counter delta across the scale-change window

metrics.label: Estimated hourly cost
metrics.howMeasured: Sum of node counts times .env PRICE_* variables, recomputed every tick, never hardcoded

phases.label: Plan
phases.narration: This is one Terraform config: a VPC, an EKS cluster, a TiDB Cloud Dedicated cluster, and the app that connects them. Let's see the plan.

phases.label: Apply: VPC + EKS + TiDB
phases.narration: Terraform is creating all of this in one run. The VPC and the TiDB Cloud cluster don't depend on each other, so they provision in parallel; EKS takes the longest because AWS has to stand up a real control plane.

phases.label: Connect app to TiDB
phases.narration: The app never touches TiDB Cloud credentials by hand. Terraform wrote the connection secret straight from its own output.

phases.label: Load burst
phases.narration: Now let's put traffic through it and watch QPS and latency.

phases.label: Scale TiDB capacity
phases.narration: We're changing TiDB's node count from 1 to 2, the smallest possible scale-out. Terraform shows this as an update, not a replace, because the provider marks node count as changeable in place.

phases.label: Verify zero downtime
phases.narration: While that scale-out ran, here's the exact request error count the load generator logged. Not an assumption, a count.

phases.label: Teardown
phases.narration: And here's the exact command and the exact check that nothing is left running or billing.

checks.label: All planned resources created
checks.description: change_summary reports remove: 0 and add equal to the planned_change count; every apply_complete resource appears exactly once

checks.label: App connected over the intended endpoint
checks.description: App's tidb_connection_target metric label matches the Terraform output connection_endpoint_kind

checks.label: Zero failed requests during scale change
checks.description: Load generator error-count delta across the scale window, reported honestly even if nonzero

checks.label: Destroy leaves zero resources in state
checks.description: terraform show -json after destroy reports no root module resources

controls.label: Plan capacity change
controls.description: Runs terraform plan -json -out=scale.tfplan with a higher tidb_node_setting.node_count

controls.label: Run load burst
controls.description: Starts a 60-second higher-rate burst against the app Service on top of steady background load
